properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Nothing here is intent, and no option is preferred.

THE OBSERVATION, dev_storyflow 2026-09-25 (storyflow #654), in their words: "when a finding names a *class* ('likely other DAGNode kinds share it'), `record_finding` could prompt for a census step. The first fix here covered only the one key I had met; a 63-type census found six more owning keys." The finding had already named the class, but nothing made anybody count its members before the fix shipped. reflow2's own record has the same shape twice. fact:six-constructors-cannot-write-any-prose-because-the-class-was-fixed-one-report-at-a-time-and-never-swept found five reported holes that were one hole across 6 of 11 constructors. fact:the-parallel-batch-class-recurred-because-only-its-instance-was-fixed found the instance fixed while the class recurred through a different pair 21 days later. The root-cause skill's step ⑥ asks WHAT class this is, and never asks HOW MANY members it has, or which were checked.

THE OPTIONS:

(a) THE REPORTER'S: record_finding's reply adds a note when the statement names a class: "name the population and count it before the fix." Cheap. The prompt lands at the moment between cause and fix.

(b) A STRUCTURED CENSUS on the finding, for example `population` (what the class ranges over) and `census` (N of M members checked, with M stated). A class finding with no census then becomes queryable, and a detector could count them the way fix_without_recorded_cause counts fixes with no cause.

(c) SKILL ONLY: one line in root-cause step ⑥: "name the population the class ranges over and enumerate it; the fix covers the census, not the instance." No tool change. (dev_storyflow keeps a rule to the same effect in its own design: enumerate the population before acting on a classification.)

(d) NOTHING. Step ⑥'s test ("would this fix have stopped the report from three weeks ago?") already implies it.

🛑 THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENTS. [1] Telling from free text that a finding "names a class" is a keyword guess. A note that fires on every "all" or "every" becomes wallpaper, the same reason /root-cause was TIERED rather than made blanket (dec:idea-root-cause-runs-at-the-moment-a-cause-is-about-to-be-written-not-on-every-failure). [2] A census's cost varies enormously: 63 node types is one script, a whole corpus is not. A prompt that cannot say how big the census is may be skipped exactly where it matters. [3] (b) adds fields the root-cause lessons already warn about: a declared field nobody writes stays empty unless all three legs (tool, instruction, detector) exist.
properties.name: OPEN — when a finding names a CLASS ("likely other kinds share it"), should record_finding (or the root-cause skill) ask for the census of that class's population before the fix, so the fix does not cover only the one member that was met?
properties.rationale: Relayed from dev_storyflow's agent sessions (art:dev-storyflow-feedback-2026-09-27, the 2026-09-25 entry) in the 2026-09-28 triage; the idea is theirs. It is worth a node because the shape it answers, a class named and only its instance fixed, is measured three times: twice on reflow2 itself and once in their 63-type census, which found six more members after the first fix. It is recorded as an idea because the trigger cannot be detected mechanically, and option (c) may deliver most of the value for none of the cost.
